issues.detail: Covers little error handling: there are no GLTFLoader error callbacks, no WebGL context-loss or unsupported-browser fallback, and no Suspense/ErrorBoundary for failed model loads in R3F.
Example 2 (data globe) is only a numbered prose outline with no runnable code, and Example 1 mutates a shared material in render and uses `as any`.

scenarios.name: r3f-sneaker-configurator-self-hosted-draco
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric most closely: it uses the `materials` object from useGLTF, calls setDecoderPath and preload, and says to run console.log(materials) to find the model-specific material name. A has the CDN and setDecoderPath parts and a more careful traverse-and-clone recolor, but it doesn't mention console.log(materials) and only suggests Blender or gltf.report to check names.

scenarios.name: vanilla-three-modern-scene-no-legacy-apis
scenarios.rationale: Both use three/addons, DRACOLoader with setDecoderPath on GLTFLoader, THREE.Timer with update()/getDelta() in setAnimationLoop, ACESFilmic tone mapping and a Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 2) cap; B's plain timer.update() is simpler and matches the rubric, while A adds timer.connect and passes the timestamp to update(), which is fine but slightly beyond the rubric, and neither response is clearly stronger on the rubric items themselves.

scenarios.name: instanced-globe-data-points
scenarios.rationale: A matches more of the rubric: it loads an earth texture and sets colorSpace to SRGBColorSpace, and it also uses a single InstancedMesh with setMatrixAt, instanceMatrix.needsUpdate and OrbitControls autoRotate. B covers the InstancedMesh and OrbitControls parts but leaves out the earth texture and sRGB colorSpace, using a plain-colored sphere instead.
